title: Minimum Array End
summary: Given the integers n and x , construct an array nums of size n where each element is a positive integer, and each element is greater than the previous one.
statement: Given the integers n and x , construct an array nums of size n where each element is a positive integer, and each element is greater than the previous one. Additionally, the bitwise AND of all elements in the array must equal x . Find the minimum possible value for the last element of nums .
constraints: n and x are positive integers.
Construct n strictly increasing positive values whose bitwise AND is x.
Return the smallest possible final value; the array itself is not returned.
hints: Every array element must contain all one-bits of x; including x itself ensures their AND has no additional forced bit.
Enumerate supersets of x by embedding the binary digits of n-1 into x’s zero-bit positions.
Scan bit positions; whenever x has zero, place the next low bit of n-1 into the answer.
Numeric order among x-supersets matches binary order of the bits inserted into the available positions, so offset n-1 yields the smallest possible n-th value.
editorial: Numeric order among x-supersets matches binary order of the bits inserted into the available positions, so offset n-1 yields the smallest possible n-th value.

tests.explanation: The three smallest supersets of binary 100 are 4,5,6, so the minimum final value is six.
Seven has all low bits set, so the next superset is fifteen and the answer is fifteen.
